method: The finished cover is the insert plus the chosen ease on both sides, and every panel adds the seam allowance to all four cut edges. The back is two rectangles the full width of the front: their combined height covers the front height plus the overlap, and each panel adds the opening hem so the turned-under edge lands on the seam line. Total fabric is the front area plus both back panels, and the length on 44 in (112 cm) fabric stacks the front and the two back panels along one width, so it is the front height plus twice the back panel height. Inputs are inches or centimetres (decimal comma accepted), inserts 2-60 in (5-152 cm), ease 0-3 in, seam 0-2 in, overlap 1-10 in and hem 0-2 in. It warns when the overlap exceeds half the front height and when a panel is wider than the fabric. It does not allow for directional prints, nap, pattern matching, shrinkage or squaring the fabric, and it is a planning estimate rather than a guarantee against a particular insert squishiness.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Cushion: an envelope-back cover overlaps two back panels so the insert can be removed without a zip or buttons.
Wikipedia, Seam allowance: the extra fabric between the seam line and the cut edge, added to every side of a pattern piece.
